tasks.short: Control access, custody, movement and disposal of proprietary materials.

steps.what: Check material records, authorised custodians and outstanding movements in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Determine handling restrictions using policies and agreements in the {DOCS}.
Approve exceptional access, transfer or disposal with the material owner.
Verify identity, inspect materials and complete the authorised physical handover.
Update custody, location and movement evidence in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Reconcile movement evidence and investigate missing receipts or overdue returns.

tasks.design: Configure custody records, access permissions and receipt capture in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with handling instructions held in the {DOCS}. A rule-based check in the {WORKFLOW} flags overdue returns and missing evidence; material owners approve exceptional access or disposal before the physical action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custody evidence and permissions were split between records, documents and physical handovers. Sensitivity decisions still needed an accountable owner.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record controls and forms can handle routine movements. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting receipts and exception checks.
tasks.still_hard: Physical verification, unclear ownership, suspected misuse and irreversible disposal remain difficult. Recording a handover does not prove it happened correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising suspicious requests and judging whether a proposed use exposes proprietary knowledge.

ambition.what: A controlled temporary-loan service for proprietary prototypes.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer custody updates and more investigation of unusual movements. Access and disposal decision rights remain with material owners.

reach.task: Capture custody evidence during material handovers.
reach.learn: Identity checks, condition recording and exception escalation.
Evidence sampling and the limits of recorded controls.

evidence.claim: Custody records, permissions and overdue-return checks can use deterministic records and workflow controls.
Physical custody and sensitive release decisions retain substantial human work.

assumptions: Proprietary materials include physical prototypes, components or tools and their handling documents.
Routine movements have defined authorisation rules; exceptional movements require owner approval.
Build ranges are indicative working days for one material group, excluding physical security upgrades.
Access estimates include GDPR review of custodian data and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which material categories require special controls.
Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} supports receipt capture and permission controls.
Who may authorise release, transfer and disposal.
Whether custody tracking introduces employee monitoring requiring consultation.
research_questions: Which receipt controls provide useful evidence without slowing physical handovers?
Can existing custody features cover the process before adding custom code?
new_work: Investigate overdue returns and unmatched receipts.
Maintain material owners and access permissions.
Test that receipt failures cannot silently close movements.
Review retention periods for custodian data.

tasks.short: Evaluate logistics technology and test improvements against operational needs.

steps.what: Read logistics publications in a web browser and save relevant technology notes.
Summarise capabilities, evidence and limitations in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Retrieved publications and announcements from an approved source list.
loop.output: A technology brief with source passages, capability claims and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for each factual claim; the logistician reviews relevance and uncertainty.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unreadable or unsupported items go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Publications describe capabilities in varied prose; fixed fields cannot reliably extract their qualifications.

steps.what: Compare options with operational volumes, costs and constraints in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree a pilot, acceptance criteria and operating limits with affected teams.
Configure a limited pilot in the {OPS_SYSTEM} against agreed acceptance criteria.
Compare pilot results with baseline costs, service and operational constraints.
Decide whether to stop, extend or fund the tested change.

tasks.design: A scheduled collector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers approved publications, and a bounded extraction loop prepares cited briefs in the {DOCS}. Deterministic comparisons join {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} data, while the {PROJECT} holds pilot criteria and decisions; managers approve pilot exposure and investment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scanning sources and building comparable pilot evidence took time. Published claims rarely matched local constraints or provided a usable baseline.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed collection and comparison reports are conventional integrations. Bounded extraction can reduce reading effort while preserving source passages for review.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier claims, integration costs and pilot results can mislead. Operational adoption and causal attribution still need direct investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which operational problem deserves a trial and judging whether a promising result will survive real working conditions.

ambition.what: A monthly evidence-based logistics pilot selection.

tasks.altitude: The logistician spends less time scanning and formatting, and more time designing useful trials. With delegated pilot limits, they can initiate small tests; investment approval stays with the logistics manager.

reach.task: Design a defensible pilot baseline and evaluation.
reach.learn: Comparison groups, seasonality and total operating cost.

reach.task: Assess integration feasibility before a pilot.
reach.learn: Interfaces, access controls and operational failure modes.

evidence.claim: ORTEC provides operational route planning, with a documented Albert Heijn deployment; this supports evaluating an existing capability.
Source collection, baseline calculations and pilot comparisons can be deterministic; technology selection still requires judgement.

assumptions: The first build covers a bounded topic and approved public sources.
The collector uses feeds or permitted downloads and requires no autonomous browsing agent.
Build ranges cover the evaluation toolkit and one small configuration pilot, not a major operational replacement.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for each pilot; employee consultation follows national rules where work or monitoring changes.
unknowns: Which operational problem has an agreed baseline.
Which publication sources permit automated retrieval.
Whether a suitable pilot environment exists.
Who holds pilot spending and operational change authority.
Whether the proposed pilot affects worker allocation or monitoring.
research_questions: Which candidate capability can be tested through existing configuration?
What evidence would distinguish sustained improvement from a temporary pilot effect?
new_work: Maintain the source list and remove weak evidence.
Review extracted claims and publication dates.
Close unsuccessful pilots and document their lessons.

tasks.short: Create and introduce logistics project plans, schedules, responsibility matrices and compliance trackers.

steps.what: Read the project brief and requirements in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved project brief, requirements register and obligation register.
loop.output: Structured deliverables, dates, constraints and source references, with unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate the schema and source references; the logistician checks ambiguities and missing requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unresolved fields remain blank and enter the planning discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative briefs contain requirements that cannot be captured reliably with fixed field mappings.

steps.what: Agree deliverables, dependencies, owners and capacity with workstream leads.
Build the work plan, dependency links and schedule in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Create responsibility and compliance matrices using templates in the {DOCS}.
Resolve conflicts and approve dates, responsibilities and compliance checkpoints.
Publish the approved baseline and configure task ownership and reminders in the {PROJECT}.
Demonstrate the planning tools and agree how workstream leads will maintain them.

tasks.design: Use configured templates and dependency scheduling in the {PROJECT}, with deterministic generation of responsibility and compliance matrices from approved inputs. A bounded extraction loop reads narrative briefs from the {DOCS}; only the sponsor's approved baseline activates assignments and reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans and matrices were maintained separately, so dates and owners drifted. Narrative requirements also needed interpretation before templates could be populated.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured scheduling already handles dependencies and reminders. Small generators and bounded extraction can connect approved inputs without building a new planning system.
tasks.still_hard: Resource commitments, hidden dependencies and conflicting obligations require discussion. A generated matrix cannot establish that all legal obligations have been identified.
tasks.human_edge: Securing credible commitments and exposing incompatible assumptions before a plan becomes a promise.

ambition.what: A lightweight project setup service for warehouse team leads.

tasks.altitude: The logistician spends less time formatting plans and more time testing dependencies and commitments. They can prepare smaller projects for approval; sponsor authority over commitments remains unchanged.

reach.task: Design reusable schedules and dependency checks.
reach.learn: Critical paths, capacity constraints and baseline control.

reach.task: Translate approved obligations into evidence checkpoints.
reach.learn: Traceability between requirements, owners and acceptance evidence.

evidence.claim: Configured scheduling, templates and deterministic generators can produce plans and matrices from approved structured inputs.
Narrative requirement extraction benefits from a bounded model loop with source references and unresolved fields.

assumptions: The {PROJECT} supports templates, dependencies and an approval state.
An accountable role supplies the approved obligation register.
The solution tracks commitments and deliverables without scoring individual workers.
Build ranges cover one project family and include access, rollout and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which planning functions are already licensed and configured.
Whether project templates and obligation registers are current.
Who can approve capacity and delivery commitments.
Whether employee consultation is required for changed task tracking.
research_questions: Can one structured project baseline replace separately maintained planning documents?
Which checks reveal missing owners or impossible dependencies before approval?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and unresolved fields.
Maintain templates and approved obligation mappings.
Check generated schedules for unrealistic assumptions.
Handle failed publication and duplicate task creation.

tasks.short: Coordinate logistics projects using technical data, progress analysis and agreed corrective actions.

steps.what: Gather shipment, cost and milestone records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {PROJECT}.
Request missing figures and explanations from workstream leads through the {EMAIL}.
Calculate schedule, service and cost variances in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare a status report and decision questions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated variance tables, unresolved data exceptions and attributed workstream updates.
loop.output: A cited status narrative and decision agenda with uncertainties marked.
loop.check: Insert numerical tables deterministically; check narrative claims against source records and review causal statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported explanations remain unresolved or use a factual template.
loop.why_not_simpler: Workstream explanations are free text and need concise synthesis; calculations and routine status fields remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss delivery tradeoffs and agree corrective actions with the project sponsor.
Record approved actions, owners and baseline changes in the {PROJECT}.
Send action summaries and due-date reminders through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} join operational, financial and milestone records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {PROJECT}, with deterministic validation and variance views in the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts the status narrative from validated evidence, while configured {PROJECT} workflows record approved actions and send reminders through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project identifiers, reporting dates and metric definitions differed across systems. Coordination relied on manually assembled reports and reminders.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and shared metric definitions can remove repeated preparation. Bounded drafting can turn attributed updates into a reviewable decision agenda.
tasks.still_hard: Late inputs, disputed causes and competing priorities remain. Reliable analysis does not itself secure resources or settle delivery tradeoffs.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting operational context, challenging optimistic explanations and negotiating corrective action across teams.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-project intervention review based on current logistics exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from report assembly and chasing updates toward diagnosing exceptions and preparing interventions. The logistician can trigger agreed escalation thresholds; sponsors retain authority over scope and resource changes.

reach.task: Explain service and cost variance without overstating causation.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, missing-data treatment and sensitivity analysis.

reach.task: Translate approved project interventions into revised operational priorities.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, dependency changes and escalation timing.

evidence.claim: Joined records, variance calculations and reminders can use deterministic integrations and configured workflows.
Narrative synthesis can assist report preparation, while causal interpretation and cross-team commitments remain human work.

assumptions: The scope is logistics project coordination rather than automated operational dispatch.
Workstream leads remain responsible for supplying explanations and correcting source records.
Approved actions are captured in structured fields; meeting discussion alone cannot trigger updates.
Build ranges cover one reporting process and include access and any employee consultation required by national rules.
GDPR controls apply to personal data; worker scoring or allocation would require a separate EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Whether shared project and shipment identifiers exist.
Which data sources provide timely, permitted exports or interfaces.
Who approves metric definitions and baseline changes.
Whether reports currently include identifiable worker performance.
Which escalation rights can be delegated to the logistician.
research_questions: Which data checks best distinguish a reporting failure from a real delivery exception?
Can existing reporting and reminder configuration cover the process before adding custom integrations?
new_work: Resolve unmatched identifiers and stale source data.
Review narrative summaries and unsupported explanations.
Maintain metric definitions and escalation thresholds.
Monitor failed updates and duplicate notifications.
Review access and retention as reporting scope changes.

role.altitude: The logistician spends less time assembling records, plans and reports, and more time investigating exceptions, testing improvements and coordinating commitments. Wider pilot or escalation authority requires explicit delegation; sensitive release and investment approvals remain with accountable owners.
reach: Logistics analysis: build defensible baselines and explain operational variance.
Project management: test dependencies, secure commitments and manage baseline changes.
Computer systems analysis: define interfaces, validation rules and failure handling.
Quality control: connect custody and compliance records to credible evidence.
skills_to_grow: Configuration of templates, permissions and approval workflows.
Data quality checks and operational metric design.
role.ambitious_version: Run a logistics improvement service that offers small teams project setup, controlled material loans and evidence-based operational pilots, using shared records and clear delegated limits.
